summary.headline: Welspun Enterprises Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 14% YoY to INR1,199 crore and EBITDA 31% to INR272 crore; FY26 order book about INR20,000 crore after Pune-Shirur win.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 14% YoY to INR1,199 crore, with EBITDA up 31% to INR272 crore (22% margin) and PAT up 54% to INR163 crore. FY26 revenue of INR3,615 crore met the INR3,600 crore guidance but was down 2% YoY, while EBITDA rose 16% to INR845 crore at a 23% margin. Key events were the Pune-Shirur elevated road LoA (about INR7,300 crore project cost) and the Panjarpur 910 MLD water treatment award, taking order additions to over INR10,000 crore in FY26 and the consolidated order book to about INR20,000 crore. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 15-20% and EBITDA margin of 18%-plus, citing geopolitical and supply-chain headwinds.

financial_highlights.metric: Net worth / cash / net debt (31 Mar 2026)
financial_highlights.value: Net worth INR3,261 crore; cash INR1,728 crore; net debt INR43 crore

segments.name: Tunnelling and Rehabilitation
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 37% YoY in FY26 on execution momentum and better project mix.

segments.name: Water (consolidated segment)
segments.commentary: Revenue declined 3% YoY, mainly from slower UPJJM execution; integrated water FY26 revenue cited at INR1,240 crore in an analyst question, and order book about INR14,000 crore including O&M of about INR5,000 crore.

segments.name: Transportation
segments.commentary: Revenue fell 17% YoY on project completions and the delay in awarding Pune-Shirur; transportation order book about INR6,000 crore including Pune-Shirur EPC value.

segments.name: WMEL (Welspun Michigan, 60%-plus stake)
segments.commentary: Rehabilitation contributed about 28% of FY26 revenue versus 17% in FY25; EBITDA margin stable at 21% and FY27 revenue growth guided at about 20%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at 15-20% (medium-term range), with management declining to guide above it.
EBITDA margin guidance of 18%-plus for the year, held below FY26's 22.5% deliberately to absorb supply-chain and cost risks.
FY27 order inflow target of INR8,000-10,000 crore, with management aiming to add it within H1 FY27; uncovered portion of FY27 guidance about 8-10%.
Pune-Shirur expected to contribute INR500-600 crore revenue in FY27 after financial closure (October/November), leaving about four months of execution.
WMEL targets over 25% revenue CAGR over the next three years; about 20% growth in FY27.
WMEL EBITDA margin expected to remain in 21-22% range or better.
Aunta-Simaria monetisation targeted within H1 FY27 subject to valuation; SNRP monetisation may slip into FY28.
Dharavi 418 MLD wastewater plant targeted for commissioning by July 2027; Bhandup 2,000 MLD by June 2029; UPJJM completion in FY27.
capex_capacity: Pune-Shirur: 53.4 km six-lane partly elevated highway (about 36 km elevated) on NH 753F, DBFOT model, 29-year concession (4 years construction, 25 years tolling), project cost about INR7,300 crore, EPC value about INR5,400 crore.
Dharavi 418 MLD multilevel wastewater plant about 65% complete; 15-year O&M to follow.
UP Jal Jeevan Mission projects about 80% complete; Bhandup 2,000 MLD about 20% complete; Panjarpur 910 MLD in early stages with mobilisation underway and advances received.
Varanasi-Aurangabad road completion targeted Q1 FY27; SNRP (Tamil Nadu/Puducherry) completion targeted Q2 FY27.
Oil and gas investment to date about INR500 crore (company share), per management.
Geopolymer lining for 17 km of Mumbai storm drains and a 2.5 km GRP trunk drain in Vadodara (about a year ahead of schedule) in progress.
demand_pricing: Consolidated order book about INR20,000 crore; FY26 order additions over INR10,000 crore including Pune-Shirur and Panjarpur.

Transportation order book about INR6,000 crore including Pune-Shirur EPC value; analyst estimate of residual SNRP and Varanasi backlog about INR500 crore (management: SNRP INR500-550 crore, Varanasi INR50-60 crore, implying figures were stated loosely).
Water order book about INR14,000 crore including about INR5,000 crore O&M; about INR9,000 crore outstanding execution.

Bid pipeline at WEL level across water transmission, large treatment, BOT roads and complex structures/tunnelling; management says the top of the canvas is about INR2 lakh crore for FY27, but it bids selectively.
Most contracts have WPI/CPI-linked escalation; BOT projects lack escalation provisions. MoRTH has allowed bitumen cost on actuals and monthly hybrid-annuity payments.
WMEL and WEL intercompany contract value about INR1,000-1,100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Expected project IRR, equity commitment and tolling economics for Pune-Shirur?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets equity IRR of 18% or more, consistent with its standard governance benchmark; detailed economics deferred to IR/CFO.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth be 25-30% given flat FY26 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: No; guidance stays at 15-20%, and management declined to guide higher due to supply-chain and labour headwinds.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise INR1,000 crore of preferential warrants with a cash-rich balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: It is an enabling approval only; INR250 crore has been received and INR750 crore can be called over 18 months. No further fundraise is anticipated in a normal scenario.

qa_highlights.question: When will Pune-Shirur construction and revenue start?
qa_highlights.answer: Financial closure is expected around October/November; about four months of execution in FY27, with INR500-600 crore revenue. Ramp-up follows the appointed date.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of geopolitical and raw-material cost pressure on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Most contracts have escalation clauses and government relief (bitumen on actuals, monthly hybrid-annuity payments); BOT contracts lack escalation; management says contingencies suffice and is guiding 18%-plus margin.

qa_highlights.question: Is the EBITDA margin guidance being lowered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 18%-plus, saying the plus could be near the current level in normal conditions or lower if disruptions persist.

risks_watch: Supply-chain disruption, bitumen and raw-material cost inflation, and labour shortages affecting FY27 execution and margins, especially on BOT projects without escalation.
Pune-Shirur financial closure timing (Oct/Nov) and its effect on FY27 revenue; the INR500-600 crore contribution depends on it.
FY27 order inflow of INR8,000-10,000 crore is needed to cover the uncovered 8-10% of revenue guidance; management would not commit to timing.
Transportation revenue may decline again in FY27 absent new projects; NHAI/MoRTH award pace remains slow.
Monetisation of Aunta-Simaria (H1 FY27, valuation dependent) and SNRP (possibly FY28); preferential warrant calls of INR750 crore over 18 months.
UPJJM slowdown and the Dharavi commissioning timeline (July 2027); Dharavi Ghatkopar tunnel awaits final High Court clearance.
summary.management_tone: Confident on execution, order book and balance sheet, but deliberately cautious on guidance: management declined to guide above 15-20% revenue growth or to reduce the 18%-plus margin floor. It was evasive on project-level detail, deferring IRR, Panjarpur and order-timing questions to IR/CFO.
key_quotes: So our guidance will stay to the range of 15%, 20% as we have always maintained and we will continue to maintain.
This is just an enabling approval. As of now, I can clarify, there is no proposal to raise this fund as we see the normal busin ess unfold.
We expect the order book to be added somewhere around INR8,000 crores to INR10,000 crores in FY27.

As a principle, we stay committed to asset monetization at an appropriate time so that we can create value for the stakeholders at the right value as well as turn the equity quickly for future growth.
